AK-GOPALAN-1950.case_title: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
AK-GOPALAN-1950.ratio_summary: Fundamental rights are separate and watertight compartments; Article 21 requires only formal procedure established by law.

SANKARI-PRASAD-1951.case_title: Sri Sankari Prasad Singh Deo v. Union of India
SANKARI-PRASAD-1951.ratio_summary: Constitutional amendment under Article 368 is constituent power and not law under Article 13(2).

SAJJAN-SINGH-1965.case_title: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
SAJJAN-SINGH-1965.ratio_summary: Affirmed Sankari Prasad, holding Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution including fundamental rights.

GOLAKNATH-1967.case_title: I.C. Golaknath v. State of Punjab
GOLAKNATH-1967.ratio_summary: Constitutional amendment is law within Article 13(2); Parliament cannot abridge Fundamental Rights.

RC-COOPER-1970.case_title: R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (Bank Nationalisation)
RC-COOPER-1970.ratio_summary: Direct effect of law on fundamental rights matters; Articles 14, 19, and 21 are not mutually exclusive.

KESAVANANDA-1973.case_title: Kesavananda Bharati Sripadagalvaru v. State of Kerala
KESAVANANDA-1973.ratio_summary: Parliament has amending power under Article 368 but cannot alter or destroy the Basic Structure of the Constitution.

ADM-JABALPUR-1976.case_title: ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (Habeas Corpus Case)
ADM-JABALPUR-1976.ratio_summary: During presidential proclamation of emergency, locus standi to move writ under Article 226 for habeas corpus remains suspended.

MANEKA-GANDHI-1978.case_title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
MANEKA-GANDHI-1978.ratio_summary: Procedure established by law under Article 21 must be just, fair, and reasonable, incorporating substantive due process principles.

SHAH-BANO-1985.case_title: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
SHAH-BANO-1985.ratio_summary: Section 125 CrPC applies to all citizens irrespective of religion; a divorced Muslim wife is entitled to maintenance if unable to maintain herself.

SURESH-KOUSHAL-2014.case_title: Suresh Kumar Koushal v. Naz Foundation
SURESH-KOUSHAL-2014.ratio_summary: Reversed Delhi High Court judgment and upheld constitutional validity of Section 377 IPC.

PUTTASWAMY-2017.case_title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
PUTTASWAMY-2017.ratio_summary: Right to privacy is a fundamental right guaranteed under Part III; explicitly overruled ADM Jabalpur and M.P. Sharma.

NAVTEJ-JOHAR-2018.case_title: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
NAVTEJ-JOHAR-2018.ratio_summary: Decriminalized consensual sexual acts between consenting adults in private; read down Section 377 IPC; explicitly overruled Suresh Koushal.

SOWMITHRI-VISHNU-1985.case_title: Sowmithri Vishnu v. Union of India
SOWMITHRI-VISHNU-1985.ratio_summary: Upheld constitutionality of Section 497 IPC criminalizing adultery against challenges under Articles 14 and 21.

JOSEPH-SHINE-2018.case_title: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
JOSEPH-SHINE-2018.ratio_summary: Struck down Section 497 IPC as unconstitutional violating Articles 14, 15, and 21; explicitly overruled Sowmithri Vishnu.

edges.treatment_context: An 11-judge bench overruled 5-judge bench in Sankari Prasad holding Article 13(2) applies to constitutional amendments.
11-judge bench in Golaknath overruled 5-judge bench in Sajjan Singh.
11-judge bench rejected mutual exclusivity doctrine formulated in A.K. Gopalan.
13-judge bench overruled 11-judge bench in Golaknath, restoring constituent amending power subject to basic structure.
7-judge bench overruled A.K. Gopalan's restrictive reading of Article 21, establishing substantive due process requirements.
9-judge bench expressly overruled ADM Jabalpur, upholding Justice H.R. Khanna's historic dissent as the true law.
5-judge Constitution bench explicitly overruled 2-judge bench decision in Suresh Kumar Koushal.
5-judge Constitution bench explicitly overruled 3-judge bench decision in Sowmithri Vishnu.
